evals.prompt:
Add Auth0 authentication to an Ionic React application with Capacitor using the @auth0/auth0-react SDK.

**Auth0 Credentials:**
- Domain: `dev-example.auth0.com`
- Client ID: `abc123def456ghi789jkl012`
evals.expected_output: Working Ionic React + Capacitor app with Auth0 login via Capacitor Browser, deep link callback handling, logout, and user profile display
expectations: Auth0 React SDK installed via any valid method (npm or yarn)
Has correct import statement for @auth0/auth0-react
Auth0 SDK initialized (Auth0Provider mounted or useAuth0 hook used)
Implements login functionality via loginWithRedirect
Implements logout functionality
Uses Capacitor Browser plugin for native browser opening
Uses Capacitor App plugin for deep link handling
Uses secure credential storage via refresh tokens (useRefreshTokens)
Auth0 domain dev-example.auth0.com written to config or source file
Client ID abc123def456ghi789jkl012 written to config or source file
No client_secret in native app
Does not use window.location.origin as redirect URI (must use custom scheme)
Correctly integrates Auth0 into Ionic React + Capacitor app with login, logout, deep link callback, and custom URL scheme
Uses current SDK version (2.16.2 or newer) in dependency declaration
Enables refresh tokens (useRefreshTokens={true}) required for Capacitor
Disables refresh token iframe fallback (useRefreshTokensFallback={false}) required for Capacitor
Calls handleRedirectCallback to process deep link auth response
Closes Capacitor Browser after handling callback
Listens for appUrlOpen deep link event from Capacitor App plugin
Uses Capacitor-specific advanced patterns: refresh token config, Browser.open in openUrl, appUrlOpen listener with handleRedirectCallback, Browser.close

Auth0 domain written to config or source file
Client ID written to config or source file

graders.question: Does the solution correctly integrate Auth0 into an Ionic React + Capacitor native mobile app with working login via Capacitor Browser, deep link callback handling via Capacitor App plugin, logout, and proper custom URL scheme configuration?
graders.examples:
PASS: Uses Auth0Provider with loginWithRedirect using Browser.open in openUrl callback, handles appUrlOpen deep link events with handleRedirectCallback, implements logout with Browser.open, and uses custom scheme callback URL.
FAIL: Only implements basic React SPA login without Capacitor Browser/App plugins.
FAIL: Uses window.location.origin as redirect URI instead of custom URL scheme.

graders.description: Enables refresh tokens (required for Capacitor - no iframe available)
Disables refresh token iframe fallback (required for Capacitor)
Calls handleRedirectCallback to process deep link auth response
Closes Capacitor Browser after handling callback
Listens for appUrlOpen deep link event from Capacitor App plugin
Uses skill-specific advanced pattern knowledge for Capacitor integration
graders.question: Check ONLY for these skill-specific advanced patterns (NOT basic SDK usage like Auth0Provider, loginWithRedirect, useAuth0). Look for at least 2 of: (1) useRefreshTokens={true} AND useRefreshTokensFallback={false} configured together, (2) Browser.open() used inside an openUrl callback parameter of loginWithRedirect, (3) CapApp.addListener('appUrlOpen', ...) with handleRedirectCallback inside the listener, (4) Browser.close() called after handleRedirectCallback. These are Capacitor-specific patterns taught by the skill that are NOT part of standard React SPA knowledge. Answer YES only if at least 2 of these advanced patterns are present, NO otherwise.
graders.examples:
PASS: Code has Auth0Provider with useRefreshTokens={true} and useRefreshTokensFallback={false} AND uses Browser.open inside openUrl callback of loginWithRedirect.
PASS: Code handles appUrlOpen deep link event calling handleRedirectCallback AND calls Browser.close() afterward.
FAIL: Code only uses basic Auth0Provider with loginWithRedirect() without any Capacitor-specific patterns.
FAIL: Code has Auth0Provider but uses window.location.origin as redirect_uri and no Capacitor plugins.
